text: Writing clean code is a crucial skill for any programmer. The goal is not just to make the computer understand your instructions, but to make the code easy for other humans to read and understand. This is often called "readability." A key part of readability is using good naming conventions. Instead of naming a variable “x” or “data,” use descriptive names like “totalPrice” or “customerList.” Similarly, you should create small, focused functions that do one specific job. This makes the code modular and easier to test. Ultimately, clean code improves maintainability, meaning it is much simpler for you or your team to update, fix bugs, and add new features without breaking existing functionality.
